scenario.title: Verification Test Setup and Reporting
scenario.initial_description: An engineer prepares a verification test, runs the evaluation, checks the results, and writes a short report. If something looks wrong, the engineer investigates and shares the result with related people.

reference_workflow.goal: Run a verification test and distribute a summarized result report.

activities.name: Review report and request clarification if needed

decisions.condition: Are the result files complete and readable?
Do the results contain abnormal patterns?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Result file collection is repetitive and follows a standard folder or repository pattern.
Completeness and basic validity checks can be rule-based.
Report drafting can be supported by template filling and result summarization.

decisions.condition: Is the investigation complete and findings ready to share?

exceptions.description: Test execution fails to complete due to environment or configuration error
exceptions.handling: Engineer reviews execution logs, corrects configuration, and re-runs evaluation

exceptions.description: Report cannot be finalized due to unresolved investigation
exceptions.handling: Report is put on hold until investigation findings are confirmed; stakeholders are notified of delay

exceptions.description: Related stakeholders are unavailable or unresponsive when findings are shared
exceptions.handling: Engineer escalates through alternative communication channel or records findings for later distribution

dependencies.note: Report and findings are both inputs to sharing step

automation_opportunities.rationale: Test execution is often highly repetitive and follows deterministic scripts; automated test runners can execute test suites without manual intervention, reducing time and human error.
required_data: Target system access credentials or interface
constraints: Test environment must be stable and accessible
Scripts must be well-defined and not require ad-hoc judgment during execution

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated result parsing and threshold-based pass/fail evaluation can flag anomalies without manual review, especially when expected outcomes are predefined.
constraints: May not handle ambiguous or novel failure modes well without human review

automation_opportunities.target: D1 - Do the results look correct?
automation_opportunities.rationale: If pass/fail criteria are quantitative and well-defined, a rules engine or statistical comparison tool can automatically route to report writing or investigation without manual judgment.
constraints: Low confidence scenarios (borderline results) may still require engineer judgment
Criteria must be formally specified in advance

automation_opportunities.rationale: Report generation can be partially or fully automated by populating predefined templates with structured test results, timestamps, and pass/fail outcomes.
constraints: Narrative commentary or contextual interpretation may still require manual input

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated notification and distribution via email or collaboration tools can be triggered upon report completion or investigation closure, reducing manual communication overhead.
constraints: Stakeholder list must be maintained and up to date
Sensitive findings may require manual review before distribution

automation_opportunities.rationale: Test preparation steps such as populating test configurations from templates or pulling requirements from a requirements management system can be partially automated to reduce setup time.
constraints: Novel or first-time test types may require significant manual design effort
Automation limited to repeatable or templated test types

assumptions: The engineer is a single actor throughout the process, though in practice multiple engineers or roles may be involved.
The term 'related people' in the original description is interpreted as stakeholders who need to be informed of investigation findings or final results.
The report writing step (A4) occurs even in the normal (no-issue) path; in the issue path, sharing findings (A6) supplements or replaces the standard report distribution.
The investigation step (A5) may iterate multiple times before findings are ready, captured via the D2 loop.
Systems referenced (e.g., Test Management Tool, Test Execution Environment) are generic placeholders consistent with common engineering workflows and are not specific to any real product.
The workflow is assumed to be linear with one main exception path; more complex branching (e.g., partial failures, multiple investigators) is not modeled due to insufficient detail.
Sharing findings (A6) is relevant both after investigation and potentially after a clean report is completed, though the primary trigger from the scenario description appears to be the issue path.
